memory_update.text: Use NVDA as the reference demand anchor for accelerator-led pull-through into HBM, advanced packaging, networking, optics, power integrity, cooling, and data-center infrastructure; do not rank it as an underfollowed discovery candidate.

Use TSM as the reference bottleneck anchor for advanced logic and CoWoS/SoIC-like packaging; smaller OSAT, substrate, test, metrology, and materials candidates should be judged by whether they benefit from TSM capacity constraints or partner outsourcing.
Use AVGO and MRVL as AI fabric and custom-silicon benchmarks for evaluating smaller optical, CPO, DSP, laser, InP substrate, and interconnect candidates.

Keep STX and WDC in the underfollowed lane only as second-order AI storage hypotheses; they are not yet chokepoint candidates unless nearline exabyte growth, pricing, and cloud/AI customer evidence separate them from normal commodity storage cycles.

This candidate chunk is reference-heavy and lacks the strongest underfollowed Layer 2A chokepoint nodes: InP substrates, T-glass, high-end MLCCs, advanced packaging OSAT overflow, probe/test, inspection/metrology, and power-conversion suppliers.
Before promotion to later layers, all six tickers need current market cap, valuation, estimate-revision, liquidity, short-interest, analyst-coverage, and primary-filing evidence checks.

For STX and WDC, the falsification plan should test whether AI/cloud demand is merely coincident with a storage cycle upturn; negative signs include weak nearline exabyte growth, falling pricing, inventory rebuild without end demand, or no cloud customer capex linkage.

summary: Layer 2B maps this candidate chunk as an AI-infrastructure relationship graph rather than a standalone ticker list. NVDA, TSM, AVGO, and MRVL are reference anchors that define demand, manufacturing, packaging, networking, optical-DSP, and custom-silicon economics. STX and WDC are underfollowed second-order storage beneficiaries, but their AI linkage is materially less direct and must be verified through nearline exabyte growth, cloud capex, pricing, and margin evidence. This chunk does not yet contain the strongest underfollowed chokepoint names from Layer 2A, such as InP substrates, T-glass, high-end MLCCs, OSAT overflow, or advanced packaging specialists; therefore the main memory update is to use the reference leaders to test second-order supplier exposure rather than treat them as alpha candidates themselves.
